title: Boolean matrix-product verification

problem.name: Boolean matrix-product verification
problem.statement_latex:
For $A,B,C\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$, decide whether $C_{ij}=\bigvee_k(A_{ik}\wedge B_{kj})$ for all $i,j$. This checks the claimed two-step reachability relation of a directed graph.
The main comparison counts Boolean matrix-entry queries; explicit classical computation also counts arithmetic or word operations.

quantum.details_latex: The 2026 algorithm reduces verification to Orthogonal Vectors and uses quantum search on structured subinstances. Its quantum lower bound is $\Omega(n^{5/4})$. Nested quantum search also supplies an $O(n^{3/2})$-query construction with a simpler implementation.
quantum.details_text: The 2026 algorithm reduces verification to Orthogonal Vectors and uses quantum search on structured subinstances. Its quantum lower bound is $\Omega(n^{5/4})$. Nested quantum search also supplies an $O(n^{3/2})$-query construction with a simpler implementation.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^2)$ entry queries; $O(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic time for computing and checking the Boolean product.
classical.details_latex: The query upper bound reads all three matrices. Exact Boolean multiplication can use algebraic matrix multiplication over a suitable field, with exponent $\omega\le9/4$, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. The problem uses Boolean-semiring multiplication; a zero output entry and a one output entry have different witness conditions.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial query improvement: $n^2\to\widetilde O(n^{17/12})$. The method combines reductions, quantum search and quantum walks.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant implementation needs coherent access to the matrices and to the records used by the Orthogonal Vectors procedure. Logical memory depends on that implementation; the simpler nested-search algorithm uses small index registers with reversible query workspace.
